# ChartBook

> A developer platform for data science teams to discover, document, and share analytics work. Provides a centralized catalog for pipelines, charts, and dataframes with automatic documentation website generation.

ChartBook organizes analytics work into **pipelines** (self-contained projects) or **catalogs** (multi-pipeline collections). All configuration uses TOML format (`chartbook.toml`).

## Quick Start

- [Getting Started](docs_src/getting-started.md): `pip install "chartbook[all]"` for everything, `pip install "chartbook[data]"` for data loading only
- [CLI Reference](docs_src/reference/cli.md): `chartbook init`, `chartbook build`, `chartbook browse`, `chartbook publish`, `chartbook catalog`, `chartbook ls`, `chartbook data`, `chartbook config`

## Guides

- [Documenting a Pipeline](docs_src/guide/documenting-a-pipeline.md): Describe charts, dataframes, and notebooks in `chartbook.toml`
- [Catalogs and Data Access](docs_src/guide/catalogs-and-data.md): Aggregate pipelines; load any cataloged dataset with `data.load()`
- [Plotting](docs_src/guide/plotting.md): One call produces interactive HTML plus static PNG/PDF
- [How the Build Works](docs_src/guide/how-the-build-works.md): Two-stage build internals and template overrides

## Reference

- [Configuration](docs_src/reference/configuration.md): Complete `chartbook.toml` reference with all fields, types, and defaults
- [Python API](docs_src/reference/api.md): `from chartbook import data; lf = data.load(pipeline="my_pipeline", dataframe="df_id")` — pipeline accepts a bare name or a scoped name (`myorg/my_pipeline`)

## Key Commands

```bash
chartbook init            # Scaffold a new pipeline project
chartbook build           # Generate HTML documentation website
chartbook build -f        # Force overwrite existing docs
chartbook browse          # Open the generated site
chartbook publish            # Stage publishable files to a directory
chartbook create-data-glimpses  # Create data summary report
chartbook config             # Configure default catalog path
chartbook catalog add <dir>  # Register a pipeline in the catalog
chartbook catalog build      # Build the catalog site
chartbook ls                 # List all pipelines, dataframes, charts
chartbook ls dataframes      # List dataframes only
chartbook data get-path --pipeline <id> --dataframe <id>   # Get parquet path
chartbook data get-docs --pipeline <id> --dataframe <id>   # Print docs content
```

## Minimal Configuration Example

All `[project]` keys are optional (an empty `chartbook.toml` is a valid pipeline manifest). Project type is inferred: a `[pipelines]` registry table means catalog, otherwise pipeline. Each chart and dataframe needs exactly one of `docs_path` (external markdown file) or `docs` (inline markdown).

```toml
[project]
name = "My Pipeline"
description = "Analytics pipeline description"
maintainer = "Your Name"

[charts.my_chart]
name = "My Chart"
description = "Chart description"
dataframe = "my_data"
path = "./_output/chart.html"
docs_path = "./docs_src/charts/chart.md"

[dataframes.my_data]
name = "My Data"
description = "Data description"
sources = ["Source"]
path = "./_data/data.parquet"
date_col = "date"
docs = "Documentation for this dataset."
```

## Directory Structure

```
my-pipeline/
├── chartbook.toml      # Configuration
├── README.md           # Required; becomes the site front page
├── _data/              # Parquet data files
├── _output/            # Generated HTML charts
├── docs_src/           # Markdown documentation
│   ├── charts/
│   ├── dataframes/
│   └── site/           # Optional custom site pages
└── src/                # Python source code
```
